reengineering.title: Driver-based budget with commitment control
reengineering.current_process: Annual static budget: departments and PDD fill templates, Finance consolidates, ManCom approves. Spending is checked against budget mainly when the bill arrives.
reengineering.pain_points: Budget is outdated within months. Overspend is found after the commitment is made. Consolidation is heavy manual work.
reengineering.proposed: Build the budget from drivers (units, prices, cost per sqm, headcount) and reforecast quarterly. Check budget availability at purchase request and reserve the amount (commitment control).
reengineering.justification: Overspend is caught before PHI is committed, not after the invoice. Reforecasting replaces most re-budgeting. Drivers make consolidation automatic and explainable.
reengineering.controls: Approved baseline locked and versioned. Realignments above threshold need DOA approval. Every override logged.
reengineering.kpi: % of POs budget-checked at request; full-year forecast accuracy
reengineering.why_problem: The budget is a once-a-year spreadsheet with no link to what PHI actually commits. Spend is checked only when bills post, after PHI is already contractually committed, so the budget reports variances but cannot prevent them.
reengineering.how_fixes: A driver model ties the budget to operational reality (units sold, cost per sqm), so a change in drivers updates the budget instead of forcing a re-budget. Checking and reserving budget at the purchase request stops overspend at the cheapest point — before a supplier is engaged.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens control: a detective check (variance after posting) becomes a preventive one (block or escalate before commitment). Baseline versions and every override are logged for audit.

reengineering.title: One digital Delegation of Authority matrix
reengineering.current_process: Sequential approval chains defined per document type (e.g., LAD Officer → Head → Legal → Finance → CFO/CEO; Dept Head → OM → Budget Authority), largely on paper and email.
reengineering.pain_points: Long cycle times. Documents wait in inboxes with no visibility of where they are stuck. Thresholds differ by department.
reengineering.proposed: One Board-approved DOA matrix by document type, amount and risk, configured once in Odoo. Independent reviews (e.g., Legal and Finance) run in parallel. Approval SLAs with auto-escalation. Low-value, in-budget items auto-approved and sampled monthly.
reengineering.justification: Removes waiting time, not controls. Every approval is visible with timestamps. One matrix to maintain instead of department-specific rules.
reengineering.controls: Requester ≠ approver enforced by the system. Thresholds set by the Board. Monthly post-approval sampling by Internal Audit. Delegations have end dates.
reengineering.sow_status: Covered (§3.4 approval matrices); PHI defines the DOA
reengineering.kpi: Median approval cycle time; % approvals within SLA
reengineering.why_problem: Approval rules differ by department and live in people's heads or on paper routing slips. Approvals run one after another even when reviewers check unrelated things, and nobody can see where a document is waiting.
reengineering.how_fixes: One matrix means one set of limits to maintain and audit. Parallel review removes queueing time without removing any reviewer. SLAs and escalation make delays visible. Auto-approval with sampling focuses senior attention on high-value, high-risk items.
reengineering.control_effect: Maintains or strengthens control: approvers and limits come from a Board-approved matrix; the system prevents self-approval; every decision is timestamped; Internal Audit samples auto-approved items monthly.

reengineering.title: Two-stage land due diligence with deal scorecard
reengineering.current_process: Due diligence on title, survey, zoning and appraisal runs largely one step after another before ManCom evaluates the deal.
reengineering.pain_points: Fatal flaws (title defects, CARP/DAR coverage, no road access) surface late, after DD spend. ManCom compares deals presented in different formats.
reengineering.proposed: Stage 1: screen knock-out criteria (title, CARP/DAR, zoning, access) within days. Stage 2: run the full DD workstreams in parallel. Present every deal to ManCom on one standard scorecard (price, yield, risks). One digital deal room per parcel.
reengineering.justification: Weak deals stop early, cutting wasted DD cost. Standard scorecards let ManCom decide faster and compare like with like.
reengineering.controls: Gate decisions recorded. DD evidence retained per parcel. Broker conflict-of-interest declarations.
reengineering.kpi: Days from opportunity logged to go/no-go; DD spend on rejected deals
reengineering.why_problem: Due diligence runs as one long sequence, so a fatal flaw (title defect, CARP coverage, no access) may only surface after surveys and appraisals are paid for. ManCom receives deals in different formats, which slows decisions.
reengineering.how_fixes: A short knock-out screen kills doomed deals within days. Running the remaining DD workstreams in parallel shortens the elapsed time. A standard scorecard lets ManCom compare deals on the same terms and decide in one sitting.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens governance: every gate decision and its evidence is recorded per parcel; broker conflicts of interest are declared up front.

reengineering.title: Evidence-based land payments and filing calendar
reengineering.current_process: Milestone payments released on request; tax filings and title transfer tracked manually.
reengineering.pain_points: Risk of paying before conditions are met. Surcharges for late filings. Little visibility of titles in transit.
reengineering.proposed: Release a milestone payment only when its evidence is uploaded and verified by Legal. Generate a statutory filing calendar (CGT, DST, transfer tax, RD) automatically at deed signing. Keep a titles-in-transit register.
reengineering.justification: Paying on evidence prevents premature payments. The calendar avoids penalties. ManCom sees which titles are at risk.
reengineering.controls: Legal verifies evidence independently of the requester. Each filing closed with proof of payment.
reengineering.kpi: Filing penalties paid; % milestone payments with verified evidence
reengineering.why_problem: Payments to landowners are released on request, so evidence that the milestone was met may be checked late or informally. Tax and title filings are tracked manually, which risks surcharges and lost visibility of titles in transit.
reengineering.how_fixes: Payment requests cannot be created until evidence is uploaded and verified. The filing calendar is generated automatically from the deed, so deadlines are never missed. A titles-in-transit register shows where every title is.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens control: pay-on-evidence is preventive; verification by Legal separates duties from the requester; each filing closes only with proof of payment (BIR, LGU, RD).

reengineering.title: Project templates and a hard License-to-Sell gate

reengineering.proposed: Project templates by type (horizontal, vertical, mixed-use) that clone WBS, cost codes, milestones and required documents. A launch gate with DP and License to Sell as hard criteria before any reservation can be made.
reengineering.justification: Setup takes hours instead of weeks, and every project reports the same way. Regulatory exposure from pre-selling is eliminated.
reengineering.controls: PD 957: system blocks reservations without an LTS. Gate approval logged.
reengineering.sow_status: Partial — LTS gate is Appendix A7

reengineering.why_problem: Each project is set up from scratch, so WBS, cost codes and documents differ between projects and cannot be compared. Selling readiness is judged case by case, which risks selling before the License to Sell is issued.
reengineering.how_fixes: Templates by project type make setup a copy-and-adjust task and guarantee the same structure across projects. A hard launch gate makes the License to Sell a system condition rather than a reminder.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens compliance: PD 957 requirement enforced by the system — no reservation can be created without an LTS. Gate approvals logged.

reengineering.how_fixes: A single cost breakdown structure used in every transaction means project P&L and cost-per-sqm benchmarks come straight from the system. Settling it before BRD avoids rebuilding reports later.

reengineering.title: Measure construction progress once, use it three times
reengineering.current_process: Contractor submits an accomplishment report, QS verifies, progress billing is processed, and unit construction status is updated separately.
reengineering.pain_points: The same progress is measured and keyed several times. Disputes over % complete. Revenue (POC) and inventory status lag reality.
reengineering.proposed: One joint site verification per billing cycle, captured on mobile with geotagged photos and % per BOQ line. The verified % drives progress billing (with retention and recoupment), unit construction status, and the POC input for revenue.
reengineering.justification: One measurement feeds three processes, removing re-keying and reconciliations. Photo evidence reduces disputes.
reengineering.controls: QS verification independent of the project team. Contractors cannot bill above verified %. Retention and recoupment computed, not typed.
reengineering.kpi: Days from cut-off to approved progress billing; billing disputes
reengineering.why_problem: Construction progress is measured separately for contractor billing, unit status and revenue, so the same fact is keyed and reconciled several times and the numbers can disagree.
reengineering.how_fixes: One verified measurement per cycle becomes the single source for billing, inventory status and revenue. Mobile capture with photos provides evidence and shortens disputes.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens control: QS verification independent of the project team; contractors cannot bill above verified progress; retention and recoupment computed by rule, not typed.

reengineering.title: Pricing governance and a single price source

reengineering.justification: Protects margin. One version of price and availability for everyone. Fewer calls to Sales admin.
reengineering.controls: System blocks under-floor quotes. Discounts beyond the matrix need DOA approval. Price changes logged.
reengineering.odoo_enabler: Pricelists, pricing rules engine, broker portal
reengineering.kpi: Average discount vs list; % of sales with exception discounts
reengineering.why_problem: Discounts are approved case by case with no consistent limits, and brokers may quote from outdated price lists, which leaks margin and creates disputes.
reengineering.how_fixes: A price floor and discount matrix set the limits once; the system enforces them. Publishing prices and availability only through the portal means everyone works from the same live data.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens control: under-floor quotes blocked; discounts above the matrix need DOA approval; every price change logged.

reengineering.title: Electronic collections with automatic bank matching
reengineering.current_process: Buyers pay at the cashier or by check/PDC. Cashier issues receipts. Posting and bank matching are manual.
reengineering.pain_points: PDC handling and bounced checks. Posting delays make SOAs stale. High cashier workload.
reengineering.proposed: Move buyers to electronic payment using per-buyer bank references (InstaPay, PESONet, bank over-the-counter). Daily bank file (CSV/MT940) auto-matched to the buyer ledger. Invoice issued on posting. Cashier handles exceptions only. No PDCs for new buyers.
reengineering.justification: Same-day posting and accurate SOAs. Fewer bounced checks. Less cash-handling risk.
reengineering.controls: Daily bank reconciliation. Separate duties for receipting, posting and reconciliation. BIR-registered invoice series (EOPT).
reengineering.sow_status: Partial — bank file import in scope; gateway out of scope (§9)
reengineering.kpi: % of collections received electronically; posting lag
reengineering.why_problem: Most payments arrive at the cashier or as checks, so posting depends on manual matching and statements of account lag reality. PDCs create handling risk and bounced-check follow-up.
reengineering.how_fixes: Giving each buyer a unique bank reference lets the daily bank file be matched to the right ledger automatically. The cashier handles only exceptions, and SOAs are current the same day.
reengineering.control_effect: Maintains segregation (receipting, posting, reconciliation by different people), adds daily reconciliation, and issues BIR-registered invoices on posting in line with EOPT.

reengineering.proposed: Workflow computes cash surrender value, deductions and commission clawback automatically. Unit re-priced and re-listed the day cancellation takes effect. Cancellation reason codes mandatory.
reengineering.justification: Inventory recycles faster. Statutory computation is consistent. Reason codes inform sales and product decisions.
reengineering.controls: Maceda computation rules locked. Refund approval per DOA. Reversal journals automatic and auditable.
reengineering.kpi: Days from effective cancellation to re-listing
reengineering.why_problem: Cancellations are computed and approved manually, then the unit is returned to inventory, so refunds and re-listing are slow and the reasons buyers cancel are not captured.
reengineering.how_fixes: The workflow computes cash surrender value, deductions and clawback in one step and re-lists the unit the day cancellation takes effect. Mandatory reason codes turn cancellations into sales insight.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens compliance: Maceda computation rules locked; refund approval per DOA; reversals posted automatically with an audit trail.

reengineering.how_fixes: Pre-qualifying at reservation and building the document pack during the equity period means the loan can be filed as soon as equity completes. A pipeline with lender SLAs makes delays visible weekly.
reengineering.control_effect: Maintains control: buyer consent for credit checks under the Data Privacy Act; lender correspondence retained; proceeds matched to the buyer ledger.

reengineering.title: No PO, no pay — with scheduled payment runs
reengineering.current_process: Requests, POs and bills processed with manual matching; payments released as prepared.
reengineering.pain_points: Bills without POs. Duplicate-payment risk. Frequent ad hoc payment runs.
reengineering.proposed: 'No PO, no pay' policy with defined exemptions (utilities, government fees). Mandatory 3-way match (PO – receipt or accomplishment – bill). Two scheduled payment runs a week. BIR 2307 generated and emailed automatically.
reengineering.justification: Fewer exceptions and less rework. Predictable cash outflow. Suppliers get 2307s without asking.
reengineering.controls: Duplicate bill detection. Payment runs approved as a batch per DOA. Tolerance limits on price and quantity variances.
reengineering.kpi: % of eligible spend on a PO; ad hoc payment runs per month
reengineering.why_problem: Bills without POs and ad hoc payment runs make spending hard to control and cash outflow hard to predict. Manual matching leaves room for duplicate payments.
reengineering.how_fixes: 'No PO, no pay' makes the PO the gate for spend. Three-way matching lets the system check quantities and prices. Two scheduled payment runs a week make outflows predictable, and 2307s go out automatically.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens control: duplicate bill detection, tolerance limits on variances, batch approval of payment runs per DOA; BIR 2307 issued consistently.

reengineering.how_fixes: Computing TORC per lot from deed values, paying agencies directly where e-payment exists, and posting the recharge to the buyer ledger automatically removes both the cash exposure and the missed recharges.
reengineering.control_effect: Strengthens control: no new advance while a liquidation is overdue; aging of unliquidated advances; computation audit trail.

sow_observations.title: Development effort versus itemized customizations
sow_observations.finding: The 100 itemized customizations total 573.12 dev-days. The two development columns in §5.1 (Dev Lead + Developer) total only 386 person-days, and §3.1 adds features not in §3.3 (land banking, supplier module, TORC budget, project P&L).
sow_observations.impact: Scope looks under-resourced by roughly a third; risk of rushed build or later change orders.
sow_observations.internal_ask: Ask the vendor to reconcile, and confirm in writing that every §3.1 and §3.3 item is inside the Fixed Base Fee.
sow_observations.letter_observation: The 100 customizations itemized in §3.3 total 573.12 development man-days. §5.1 allocates 386 person-days to development (Dev Lead 285 + Developer 101), which is 187.12 person-days fewer. §3.1 also describes features that have no line in §3.3, including the land banking register and carrying cost ledger, supplier accreditation and performance rating, the TORC budget rule builder and the project P&L.
sow_observations.letter_request: Please reconcile §3.3 with §5.1, and confirm in writing that every feature described in §3.1 and §3.3 is delivered within the Fixed Base Implementation Fee, without drawing on any Flex Allocation.

sow_observations.title: Man-day rates
sow_observations.finding: Base effort priced at PHP 10,000/day (739 × 10,000 = 7.39M); flex, overages and replenishments at PHP 12,000/day.
sow_observations.impact: Gaps found in this analysis would be priced at the higher rate.
sow_observations.internal_ask: Negotiate the gap items into base scope before signing, or lock CRs at 10,000.

sow_observations.letter_request: We request that the PHP 10,000 rate apply to Flex Allocations and Change Requests throughout implementation and the 90-day hypercare period.

sow_observations.title: Payment milestone weighting
sow_observations.finding: 50% (PHP 3.695M) is billed by BRD sign-off, before any build; 80% before go-live.

sow_observations.letter_request: We propose linking more of the fee to tested functionality, for example: Kickoff 15%, BRD sign-off 20%, SIT completion 25%, UAT sign-off 20% and Go-Live 20%. Please also confirm how the additional discount is applied to each milestone invoice.
